strategies.name: support_bounce_scalp_to_resistance
strategies.entry_summary: After the first 5 to 15 minutes, identify a support level on the 5-minute chart, using price action and moving averages such as the 13 EMA or 200 EMA. Enter a scalp when price comes down into that support and bounces.
strategies.exit_summary: Take profit quickly at the next resistance or after the short upward move; the speaker repeatedly frames this as getting in at support and selling at resistance without overstaying.

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: let the first 5 to 15 minutes establish support, then buy the touch/bounce off the 13 EMA
variants.target_note: exit on the quick move up / at resistance
variants.transcript_quote: this 13 EMA operated as a initial support

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: buy the bounce after the 13 EMA loses support and price finds deeper support at the 200 EMA
variants.target_note: ride it to resistance and exit
variants.transcript_quote: you get in here as support and you ride it to resistance and you exit

strategies.name: support_breakdown_short_scalp
strategies.entry_summary: When an established support level, specifically the 200 EMA in the example, is finally lost, enter in the direction of the breakdown to catch the larger downward scalp move.
strategies.exit_summary: Exit into the ensuing sharp drop after the breakdown; the speaker indicates taking the move down quickly rather than holding long-term.

result.enumeration_note: Enumerated two strategies because the video teaches both a long support-bounce scalp and the opposite breakdown move after support is lost; the latter has a concrete entry on loss of 200 EMA support and a quick exit into the down move, though its exit is described less precisely than the long setup.
